headline: Microsoft is reportedly weighing whether to delay or scale back its pledge to match all its electricity use with clean power every hour by 2030.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 2: the report is from 6 May 2026, EnergyNow re-dated it to 11 Oct, and we found no later decision.
importance_line: It matters to people who live near new data centres and to climate groups tracking big-tech pledges, then to regulators and utilities planning for the new demand, but Microsoft has announced no change and the report rests on internal discussions.
summary: Bloomberg reported on 6 May 2026, as relayed by TechCrunch, that Microsoft is debating internally whether to delay or scale back its pledge to match 100 percent of its hourly electricity use with clean power on the same grid by 2030, apparently because its rush to build AI data centres has put the goal under strain. Microsoft has announced nothing and declined to comment on the debate, though a spokesperson told TechCrunch the company continues "to look for opportunities to maintain our annual matching goal", a looser pledge that counts clean power bought over a whole year rather than matched hour by hour.
notes: Old news re-dated by EnergyNow (URL /2026/05/); hold back. Text read at TechCrunch (6 May 2026), which credits Bloomberg; the url is Bloomberg's original, decoded from Google News and not opened.
